audit_metadata.title: P3 Team-State Impact Real-Match Validation and Audit

non_striker_dynamics_audit.summary: Non-striker dynamics explicitly decouple individual execution from partner contribution.
key_findings: Batter carrying partner (share >= 65%, SR >= 130, partner SR <= 115) triggers +0.30 synergy bonus and high z_partner (+1.0 to +1.2).
Partner faster contributor penalizes slower batter with negative z_partner (-0.5 to -1.0), restraining P3.
Mutual acceleration triggers +0.20 synergy bonus for collective aggressive pacing.
Observation: In 1st innings when macro EFS surges massively due to partner explosion, 45% weight on z_macro can override negative z_partner.

failure_a_macro_tailwind.description: Low individual impact (<=15 runs, P2<=40) receiving P3>=70 due to large team macro acceleration.
failure_a_macro_tailwind.cause: 45% weight on z_macro allows strong team surge to elevate batter with negative z_partner.

failure_b_death_rrr_blowout.description: High individual impact (>=40 runs, SR>=140, P2>=75) receiving P3<=40 in steep chases.
failure_b_death_rrr_blowout.cause: Death overs RRR explosion (e.g. needing 24 off 4 balls = 36 RRR) creates large negative required_rr_change, overwhelming heroic batting.

failure_c_collapse_entry_artifact.description: Batter entering during collapse receiving high P3 without scoring runs.
failure_c_collapse_entry_artifact.verdict: Condition overs_per_wkt_entry >= 1.8 AND actual_runs >= 20 strictly prevents unearned collapse credit.

failure_d_dominant_position_artifact.description: Batter entering in dominant position receiving high P3 without contributing.
failure_d_dominant_position_artifact.verdict: Zero unearned credit; team RR baseline prevents free-riding.

failure_e_partner_acceleration_coattails.description: Anchor batter scoring at <115 SR receiving P3>=60 because partner scored 40+ runs at 160+ SR.
failure_e_partner_acceleration_coattails.cause: Team EFS/trajectory surge (z_macro) partially spills over into anchor's P3 despite negative z_partner.

failure_f_losing_team_suppression.description: Losing-team batter scoring 50+ runs at 140+ SR receiving P3<=35.
failure_f_losing_team_suppression.cause: Directly linked to Failure B in lost chases where RRR becomes mathematically impossible at exit.

failure_g_winning_team_low_effort_inflat.description: Winning-team batter scoring <=15 runs at <90 SR receiving P3>=60.
failure_g_winning_team_low_effort_inflat.cause: Comfortable chase completion gives positive target progress and small positive macro relief.

failure_h_p2_duplication.explanation: P2 and P3 share ~53% common variance while maintaining 47% independent variance. P2 measures individual execution efficiency, while P3 measures situational team-state movement.

overall_verdict.summary: The Phase 7E audit demonstrates that P3 (Team-State Impact) performs robustly on real IPL innings. It successfully rewards meaningful team-state improvements (EFS change, RRR relief, collapse stabilization, partnership carrying) while maintaining strict outcome invariance (corr with winning = 0.27). Non-striker dynamics, collapse consolidation, and mutual acceleration behave sensibly. Two minor observations were identified for potential future fine-tuning: (1) Death-overs chase RRR blowout can over-penalize heroic lone-warrior innings in lost chases, and (2) 45% z_macro weight occasionally allows an anchor to inherit macro tailwinds from an explosive partner. The production model remains completely untouched.
recommendations_for_future: Cap death-overs required_rr_change penalty when balls remaining <= 12 and batter SR is elite.
Consider increasing z_partner penalty weight relative to z_macro when partner outscores batter by >2.5x.
